**The rest of the 64 bytes over pbrt, each a decision for the user:**

- *The record's slots as a struct of arrays* (VisibleSurface 96 bytes
  of AoS stride, 81 written; pbrt's `pixelSampleState` is an SOA). Step
  6's rule extended from the cut's set to the record: `q_<local>_slots :
  T[n]` becomes one array per leaf by `leaves_of`, and the `mut T*` the
  chain is handed becomes a pointer per leaf, as 4.5's step 4 already
  does for the cut's values; every `ptr(visible, k)` and whole-value
  store through it rewritten to the leaf's. The sampler state (`st`) the
  same. The bytes do not change; the sectors per store do, and the
  padding (15 bytes) goes.
- *`lambda` beside the visible surface, as pbrt keeps it* (`pixelSample-
  State.lambda` is its own array; `visibleSurface` is initialized only
  `if (initializeVisibleSurface)`). Ours puts the wavelengths inside
  VisibleSurface (render.bonsai, the comment above the element) and so
  initializes n, ns, albedo and set for every pixel sample of every
  film: 41 bytes pbrt does not write for an RGB film. The program change
  needs a `mut` whose initializing store is under `film_visible_surface`
  -- a declaration without an initializer, or an equivalent -- which is
  a language question.
- *`prev_ctx` at the camera push* (48 bytes of a constant pbrt leaves
  unwritten). The drain reads it only under `depth > 0`, and the camera
  push stores `depth = 0`; a push whose constants make a field's every
  read dead need not store it. That is a per-push-site read analysis --
  the callee's `read_paths` under the push's constant arguments, with
  the branches those constants decide folded -- a compiler mechanism of
  the kind step 1 was, exact and not a heuristic, but new.
- *`wave`* (4 bytes): step 4, the round-uniform field.
- *The 3-vectors as three arrays on the GPU.* The 10-11 ruling keeps a
  short vector one packed array ("one store to one cache line"), true
  per thread; across a warp a 12-byte stride is three stores touching
  twelve sectors each against three touching four for pbrt's x, y, z
  arrays. Same bytes, three times the requests, for `o` and `d` of every
  ray and the three vectors of every context. The user's rule to revisit
  with this measurement in hand.
- *The `ran` byte stored twice*: one byte and one instruction; the
  atomic between the two stores is what stops LLVM's dead-store pass.

### Every induced storage a struct of arrays (10-12, 12:00-)

**The ruling (10-12, 11:50).** Put to the user as a decision, the record's
slots as a struct of arrays got a correction: "I already told you to
default to a SoA for all induced storage!" -- the 10-11 ruling for the
cut's stored set was for every array the compiler makes -- and a design
point: "it is ideal if there is some convenient 'handle' or 'cursor' to
this storage object, so we can later manipulate the layout. Probably
using the name of the stored thing." And the question "Are there any
other induced arrays?"

**The inventory** (every `make_alloca` of a generated name in src/SSA):
the queue's entry arrays (SoA since the first deferral) and its header
struct `<q>_queue`; the cut's set (SoA since 28bd4aac); the record of a
deferral -- a mutable local's slot `<q>_<local>_slots : T[n]`, a reducer's
slot, a continuation's record value `<q>_rest_<v>`, the path's result
`<q>_result`, the `ran` byte -- each one array of the stored type, *an
array of structs where T is one*; a loop interchange's expansion of a
value per outer iteration, `<name>!expanded : T[n]` (SSA/ReorderLoops.cpp),
the same; a loopify's stack `!stack : T[size]` (SSA/QueueRecursion.cpp),
one struct per entry, which is a thread's own stack indexed by depth and
not storage indexed by a parallel iteration -- a struct of arrays across
the depth would gain nothing and cost address arithmetic, so it is left
as it is and said so here. In the renderer the record was the one array
of structs: `rays_visible_slots : VisibleSurface[n]`, 96 bytes of stride
per pixel sample, every one of its eight stores from a warp touching 32
half-filled sectors where a store into an array of the field touches
four, and read back whole by the rest pass.

**Built: SSA/InducedStorage.h.** The transforms register what they make
in `Function::induced` under a handle named for the stored thing --
`rays.visible`, `rays.l`, `rays.rest.<value>`, `rays.result`, `rays.ran`
(SSA/Defer.cpp), `rays.vol_ray_samples` for the cut's set, already split
(SSA/Stage.cpp), `<name>!expanded` (SSA/ReorderLoops.cpp, whose
`reorder()` is now told, as a deferral is, whether a gang touches the
function) -- as the one array of the stored type each rewrite is simplest
with, and `split_induced_storage()` runs once every directive has run,
after the block accumulates and before the hit continuations (the
closest-hit program's parameters mirror the owner's values by name, so
the owner is split first). It replaces each array by one per leaf of the
stored type -- `leaves_of`'s rule: a scalar, a short vector kept whole
where no gang touches the queue (stored_vector_type), a bool a byte of
its own since a slot is written field by field, an ADT's padding nowhere
-- and rewrites every use of its elements' addresses by name, wherever
the threading carries it: the owner's whole store of an initializer into
a store per leaf (take_apart), the slot address a drain rebuilds from the
entry's index into an address per leaf, every chain function's `rec : mut
Record` parameter into a pointer per leaf in the parameter's place at
every call (so arguments and parameters stay in step whatever order the
splits run in -- `visible : mut VisibleSurface` through 17 functions of
the renderer), a field's address (`field.ptr(visible, 3)`) into the
leaf's, a whole load into the leaves rebuilt or, when the program only
picks fields of what it loaded (`rec.hits`: a load of the whole and a
LoadField), into each field's leaves alone, an accumulate into the one
leaf it adds into. A leaf nothing reads is then stored nowhere and has no
array: its stores, its arrays and the parameters made for it go (pbrt's
`visibleSurface` untouched for an RGB film is the case this is for, once
the initializer is conditional -- the next section). An address the
rewrite cannot follow -- compared, returned, stored as a value, a varying
argument of a run of calls -- is an error naming the function, block and
instruction, never a silent array of structs. The post-schedule dump
lists each function's storage by handle (`; storage rays.visible :
VisibleSurface as rays_visible_n_slots, ...`), which is what a later
directive takes to lay one out otherwise; nothing here is the layout
language's promise. The entry still carries the slot's index and nothing
else of the frame. Tests: ssa/defer-record-soa (a `mut Record` of a
3-vector, a float nothing reads, an int and a bool handed down a deferred
recursion: three arrays, `step` taking three pointers, the drain
rebuilding three addresses from the index, the rest pass reading each
leaf from its own array, no array and no store for `w`), its llvm golden,
and correctness/llvm and correctness/gpu twins run (1, 3, 5, 7, 5, 7, 9,
11 on the host and on the device). No existing golden moved -- none had a
record slot of struct type, which is how the array of structs went
unnoticed. The non-GPU suites pass (1534), the GPU suite (66).

**In the renderer:** `rays.visible` is six arrays -- the two normals as
packed 3-vectors, the albedo and the two halves of the wavelengths as
16-byte vectors, the set byte -- all six read (the film reads every one).
The camera kernel (SASS, sm_120) writes the record in nine stores into
arrays at 12- and 16-byte strides, three of them 128-bit, where it wrote
eight into the 96-byte struct: STG.E x28, STG.E.128 x9, STG.E.64 x2 ->
STG.E x32, STG.E.128 x9, STG.E.64 x0 per pixel sample; per warp roughly
half the sectors for the record's part of the traffic (the two 3-vectors
at a 12-byte stride are twelve sectors a store, the one thing left of the
old shape -- the 3-vectors as component arrays, the item above). The
material kernels' `visible = seen` under `want_visible` is seven stores
into the six arrays, the rest pass's reads one load per leaf.

### The wavelengths beside the surface, and the surface's initialization (10-12, 14:00-)

**The ruling (11:50):** "Regarding the wavelengths beside the surface: we
should follow PBRT's design! This is supposed to be a faithful
translation of their implementation into Bonsai. The surface
initialization only for a gbuffer film smells like we aren't using
specialize() where we need to yet, am I right?"

**Built, the program's part.** pbrt's `PixelSampleState` keeps `lambda`
as an array of its own beside `visibleSurface`; the camera kernel writes
it, the material kernel rewrites it when a dispersive interface
terminates the secondary wavelengths, the film converts with it. Ours
kept the wavelengths inside `VisibleSurface` (the comment above the
element argued for it) and so wrote the whole surface for every film.
Now `path_lambda : mut SampledWavelengths = lambda` is a local of the
pixel sample in `render`, handed down the chain beside `visible` through
the 17 functions that carry the surface (every `visible : mut
VisibleSurface` parameter gained `path_lambda : mut SampledWavelengths`,
every call hands both), the four `visible.lambda = lam` writes are
`path_lambda = lam`, the film reads `path_lambda`, and `VisibleSurface`
is pbrt's: `{n, ns, albedo, set}`. The gbuffer's accumulation is under
`film_visible_surface && visible.set`, as only a GBufferFilm has
`AddSample` read the surface. With the record a struct of arrays
(above), `rays.visible` is four arrays and `rays.path_lambda` two 16-byte
vectors, the same bytes in the same number of arrays; the change is
faithfulness, and what it sets up. In the assembly (sm_120) the camera
kernel's stores are what they were (STG.E x32, STG.E.128 x9, STG.E.U8
x4), the rest pass gains the one branch on the film's flag, and the
material kernels store two 128-bit vectors fewer under `want_visible`
(Diffuse: STG.E.128 x11 -> x9), since the surface they fill no longer
carries the wavelengths -- pbrt's material kernel writes the two apart as
well.

**Measured (10-12, 15:15-15:45, `compare-out-lambda`, with the layout
alignment below, which changes nothing of this renderer's kernels):**
the five scenes at 16 and 64 spp against `compare-out-soa`, pbrt --gpu
rerun beside ours, the least of three on each side. Kernel milliseconds,
record -> this: killeroo-simple 28.29 -> 28.41, killeroo-gold 69.43 ->
69.94, book 85.68 -> 85.59, lte-orb-silver 81.24 -> 79.80,
lte-orb-rough-glass 201.02 -> 199.81 at 16; 113.18 -> 113.06, 277.29 ->
278.86, 341.77 -> 341.60, 324.93 -> 319.15, 801.77 -> 799.08 at 64:
**1.003x kernel as a geometric mean at both counts, within the run-to-run
noise**, lte-orb-silver 1.018x at both (the material kernels' two stores
fewer), the others within a percent either way; all ten radiance images
byte-identical to heatmap5's. Faithfulness bought for nothing, as it
should be; the bytes the initializer still writes for an RGB film are the
decision above.

**The initialization, and the specialize question -- the honest answer
is "partly".** pbrt writes `pixelSampleState.visibleSurface[pixelIndex]
= VisibleSurface()` under `if (initializeVisibleSurface)`, a runtime flag
of the integrator; our `visible : mut VisibleSurface = {zero3, zero3,
zero4, false}` is unconditional, since a `mut` local has to be
initialized where it is declared: 41 bytes of stores a pixel sample that
an RGB film never reads. `specialize()` on `film_visible_surface` makes
the flag a constant in each copy of the pixel loop, but the record is one
storage shared by every copy of the loop (the seven sampler copies share
`rays_visible_slots` today, and the 14 copies would), and the rest pass
reads the surface under the flag at run time; so the unread rule, which
drops a leaf only when *nothing* reads it, sees the gbuffer copy's reads
and keeps the arrays, and the RGB copy's initializer keeps its stores.
Three honest ways to pbrt's effect, none built, each a decision:

- *Specialize before the deferral* (`render[VolPath].specialize(
  film_visible_surface)` ahead of `queue`/`defer`), so that each copy of
  the loop gets a queue, a record and drains of its own: the RGB copy's
  record is read by no film and the unread rule drops its surface
  entirely (the arrays, the parameters, the material kernels' stores
  through them). Exact, no new mechanism -- and twice the device code:
  every drain and material kernel once per film kind, pbrt's one set
  made two. pbrt does not specialize on the film; it branches.
- *A declaration without an initializer*, `visible : mut VisibleSurface;
  if film_visible_surface { visible = {...} }`, with a read of an
  unassigned field undefined, as pbrt's C++ is. The literal translation
  of pbrt's line; a language addition (the unassigned read's semantics,
  and a definite-assignment check cannot prove these reads safe, since
  the film reads under the same runtime flag that guards the write).
- *pbrt's `set` flag as the tag of an ADT*, `VisibleSurface = Empty |
  Seen{n, ns, albedo}`: the initializer stores the tag alone (an ADT's
  payload for a variant without fields is padding, stored nowhere), the
  material kernel stores `Seen` under `want_visible` as it does now, the
  film matches. One byte a pixel sample for every film, no language or
  schedule change, and `set` *is* a tag -- a VisibleSurface starts out
  empty and the integrator that fills one marks it.

The recommendation is the third; the user's call. The specialize is
right for the sampler, whose dimensions the draws depend on; for the
film it reaches the stores only by splitting the queues.

**The user's decision (10-12, 16:40): the first way, built cleanly.** "I
think we need some sort of intelligent mechanism for tracking
specializations and queues with specializations. There can (and should?)
be two different queues based on this specialization. Queues should work
with a continuation afterwards. ... Reading unwritten data is undefined
behavior and should be documented as such, but I think if we specialize
before the deferral then we don't even need to implement that, right?"
Right: with the loop specialized before the deferral, the RGB arm's record
is read by no film and the unread rule drops its surface, initializer
included. The third way is withdrawn besides: a variant's value is lowered
to a tag and a vector of zero-filled 32-bit words with the member written
over them (Lower/ADTs.cpp), so an `Empty` would store every word.

**Built: a queue on a specialized loop is one queue per arm**
(docs/schedule-semantics.md 4.6; SSA/Convert.cpp `queue_arms`,
`chain_functions`, `arm_chain_copies`, `arm_copy_of`; QueueSpec::variant
and ::region_entry). The queue directive's loop is resolved with every
copy an earlier specialize made (`p_band!VolPath` -> `p_band!VolPath!True`,
`!False`), and the deferral, the cut and the splits are applied once per
copy: a queue `rays!True` owned by the arm's loop, its record, its drains
and its rest pass under the arm, the rest loop named `rays_rest!True` so
that `bind(rays_rest, ...)` finds every arm's and `bind(rays, ...)` does
not bind it. The chain is made the arm's: a function the specialize
already copied for the arm (handed the key: `integrator_li!True` and
everything `want_visible` reaches) is used; a chain function the key never
reaches -- one that reaches the callee by calls or pushes onto the queue,
`vol_exit` -- is cloned under the arm's variant and the arm's calls
retargeted, since two arms' drains hand the chain two queues of two types;
a function off the chain stays one. A queue on `root` of a specialized
owner has an arm per variant of the owner's outermost loops, the arm's
region beginning at the loop copy the dispatch enters (QueueSpec::
region_entry). An arm that never calls into the chain gets no queue (the
integrator arms). The storage pass learned that two records handing one
function the same parameter share its reads (SSA/InducedStorage.cpp,
`shared`), so a leaf read through a shared pointer is kept for both.
report_stages.py's kernel patterns take the arm's suffix. Tests:
ssa/defer-under-specialize (two queues under `if (gbuffer)`, the False
arm's record one array, `step!True` with three pointers and `step!False`
with one), its llvm golden, correctness/llvm and correctness/gpu twins
running both arms (1 3 5 7 5 7 9 11 and 1 2 3 4 1 2 3 4). Two things
the renderer taught on the way: a loop copy's suffix is an arm's only
when it is made of the owner's specialize labels (`!False`), not another
directive's product (`!False!prologue`, the interchange's prologue; a
split's `hits!Big` drain), which is what `specialize_labels` and
`arm_suffix` decide; and `clone_function` dropped a call's `spawned`
flag, so an arm copy's `spawn l += escaped_contribution(...)` read as a
call with a rest to stage -- fixed in SSA/CloneFunction.cpp. The
renderer's schedule gains `render[VolPath].specialize(film_visible_surface)`
ahead of the queues. Compiled: `rays!False.visible : VisibleSurface as
nothing (unread)` -- the RGB arm's record has no surface storage at all --
and `rays!True.visible` the four arrays; 102 device kernels against 52
and twelve OptiX modules against six (each drain, material kernel and
program once per film kind), and the RGB arm's camera kernel writes
STG.E x26, STG.E.128 x8, STG.E.U8 x3 where the morning's wrote x32, x9,
x4: the two normals, the albedo and the set byte gone, 41 bytes a pixel
sample, pbrt's `if (initializeVisibleSurface)` as code that is not there.
One cosmetic thing left as it is: the original of a function the
deferral clones per arm (`vol_exit` beside `vol_exit!True` and `!False`;
`step` in the test) stays in the printed program with nothing calling
it, as the original of a function `specialize()` copies does already
(`integrator_li` beside `integrator_li!VolPath`); none of them reaches
the device code (the 102 PTX entries are all arms' kernels), so it costs
nothing at run time or in ptxas. A pass dropping every function no
export reaches would tidy the post-schedule dump for both.

The suites found one thing (19:20). tests/bonsai/error/
defer-callee-specialized expected `step.defer(finish, q)` refused when a
queue's specialize upstream had copied `finish` to `finish!Big` (`step`
hands it the key `hits` goes by); with the arms it compiled, because the
walk from the queue's owner resolves the callee to the copy the chain
calls, and in that program only the Big drain calls finish. The program
it built is right: `step!after!Big` pushes onto `q`, `q`'s drain calls
`finish!Big`, its rest pass writes `hits`' result for the Big entries, the
Small drain computes its own -- which is what e9ed71c1 says the schedule's
name for a function means (the function, its continuations and the copies
a queue's specialize made of it). But the walk kept the first copy it
found, so a program whose Small drain also calls finish deferred
`finish!Big`'s call and left `finish!Small`'s as it was, silently, where
the old check refused. Now `arm_chain_copies` hands back every copy of a
chain function the arm calls, `one_copy` says whether a set is one
function with the continuations split off it (`step` with `step!after`,
`vol_path_step!True` with `vol_path_step!True!after!hit`) or two copies in
their own right, and the deferral refuses two with the old message. The
error test is now the two-copies program; ssa, backends/llvm and
correctness/llvm defer-callee-copied are the one-copy program (out: -1 0
1 2 3 3.5 4 4.5). A debt found on the way, not fixed here: my first
scratch version of the two-copies program made `finish` call itself on
Small, and `specialize_callees` (SSA/Specialize.cpp) followed the
self-call -- `finish!Small`, `finish!Small!Small`, ... -- until the stack
ran out, which means a terminating recursive function handed the key it
recurses with (a tree walk passing a variant down) would be cloned
without end too; the fix is to skip a copy's call of itself there, since
specialize_function has already retargeted it, with a test of such a
function under a queue's specialize.

**The first compare of the arms build failed (20:05), and found two
bugs.** Every image was dark but for the light itself and a sprinkle of
noise (killeroo-simple at 16 spp: 1,464 pixels lit against pbrt's
488,450), and the kernels were a third slower. Emission reached the film
at every depth, so paths ran; the direct lighting did not, so the shadow
rays were the suspect, and the dump showed why: the two have_media
copies of the False arm's shadow drain (`shadow!False!drain!False`,
`!True`) each held a launch gate `dispatch have_media [exit, launch]` --
GateDrains' gate, which skips a drain whose queue cannot have been fed
-- and in a scene without media the specialize picks the have_media=False
copy and the gate then skips it. The gate was `have_media` because the
pass had found only the medium kernels' pushes onto `shadow!False`: the
split records (`hits.specialize(material)`) carry the declared name
`hits`, the pass matched a drain's family to a split by exact name, and
the arm queues `hits!False` and `hits!True` matched nothing -- their 22
leaf drains collapsed into one unsplit family, their indexed pushes
resolved to no leaf, the queues came out unfeedable (launched anyway, by
the pass's rule for that), and the material kernels' pushes onto the
shadow queue fed nothing downstream (BONSAI_DEBUG_GATES confirmed it:
`split hits drained ''`, 22 pushes to `hits!False[k]` unresolved). Fix
(SSA/GateDrains.cpp): a split is of every family named `hits` or
`hits!<arm>`, each with the split's leaves under it, the arms sharing the
one mask; the leaf labels are looked for in a loop's name after the arm's
own label. The second bug the test for the first found: for a queue on
`root`, the arm's chain was walked from the arm's loop body alone, and
the drains of the arm's earlier queues -- which a root queue puts beside
the loop, under the arm's selector -- were not walked, so a chain
function called from a split's drains kept its original (`shade!False!
Matte` calling `wetten`, not `wetten!False`) and that call was never
deferred: the right answer, computed inline, through no queue. The
renderer's queues are on `p_band`, whose drains lie inside the band loop,
so the walk reached them there; the root form has QueueArm::region now
-- the blocks only this arm's selector reaches -- and walks it.
Tests: ssa and correctness/llvm gate-drains-under-specialize (a split
queue under arms, `soaks` fed by its leaves' drains and by a drain the
producer feeds under `wet`: the leaves gated on their bits of the shared
mask, `soaks` on `wet` OR the bits; 189.5, 222, 8189.5, 8222, where the
bug printed 157 for the dry scenes). On the renderer: the hits leaves
gated per arm again, the shadow drains ungated, their trace loops
present. Two debts the GPU twin of that test found, besides the
specialize_callees one above -- all three reproduced with the compiler of
29e15282, before the arms (a build of that commit, 21:45), so none is the
arms' (each is a program with its expected output in tests/bonsai/pending,
with a README that says where each lives in the compiler): an `atomic
total += x` into a `reduce(+)` parameter, inside a function a GPU-bound
loop calls, printed 1.0 for 65 -- SSA/DemoteAtomics.cpp ran per function
and asked which bound loops of that function enclose the accumulate; in
the callee there are none, contention_of answered Disjoint, the `atomic`
came off, and the kernel's threads raced on one word (the statement
written inline in the loop keeps its atomic and the block reduction, and
prints 65; a plain `+=` is the program's own race, which is what my first
version of this test wrote, in the called form and in the gate test run
on the GPU, and the user caught). FIXED (23:55): which functions the
bound loops call is settled over the whole program first
(functions_called_in_parallel, SSA/Contention.h: the callees of blocks a
bound loop encloses, and theirs in turn), and in such a function an
atomic comes off only for storage the call made for itself (an
allocation of the function); a parameter's address is some caller's, and
whether two iterations hand down the same one is not visible from
inside, so the atomic stays -- a device atomic, `atom.relaxed.gpu.global.
add.f32`, where the loop's own body gets the block reduction. The
renderer's film atomics and wosx's walk sums sit in the bound loop's own
function, so nothing of theirs changes: the suites pass with no golden
touched (1550 non-GPU, 68 GPU). Tests: correctness/gpu/reduce-param (65)
with backends/ptx/reduce-param, and demote-atomics-callee in ssa,
backends/llvm and correctness/llvm (the reducer handed down two calls
kept, the call's own local and a callee of an unbound loop demoted, one
parallel caller enough). The gate test's GPU twin now prints 157, 157,
8157, 8157 -- its written atomics right (the squares and values; the
first run printed 12) and every spawned soak lost, for two reasons that
are not this pass's: the drain adds a spawned call's value with the
program's flag, and `spawn` has no `atomic` spelling (the parser's
`spawn` form passes atomic=false), so a spawn into the owner's reducer
from a bound drain is a race the program cannot say; and the entry of a
spawned call holds the reducer's *address*, which on the JIT runtime's
GPU path is the address of that launch's device copy of `total`
(runtime/bonsai_cuda.h, "Memory": a buffer is allocated, copied in,
copied back and freed per launch), dead by the soaks kernel -- the guard
at CodeGen_GPU_Host.cpp:304 refuses a queue struct holding such
pointers but not a record array of them. Both for the user to rule on.
(10-13, 13:00) The user: spawn expresses possible parallelism, like
parfor; a spawned function writing a reducer must write it atomic; a
safety pass should check atomics are used right under spawn and parfor;
the demotion should take an atomic off when a spawn is not parallelised.
docs/parallel-semantics.md states it formally -- activities (parfor
fork-join, spawn a deferred task that never interleaves its spawner,
joined where the reducer is read), happens-before, races as undefined,
the rule, what a schedule may do, the check (to build: every parfor and
spawn taken as parallel, a plain accumulate into a Shared reducer
refused) and the demotion (built: the schedule's forks only) as one
analysis asked two questions -- and tests pin the demotion's side today:
one program under five schedules (`wet` spawned per iteration writes
the run's reducer; `step` writes it too), ssa demote-atomics-spawn-inline/
-drain/-bound, backends/llvm -drain/-bound, backends/ptx + correctness/gpu
demote-atomics-spawn (97.5, eight ones; both `atom.*.add.f32` kept),
correctness/llvm -inline/-drain: both atomics off under no schedule and
under a sequential drain, `step`'s on and `wet`'s off with the loop bound
and the drain not, both on with everything bound. The check's side is
four pending programs with proposed diagnostics (tests/bonsai/pending/
race-parfor-reducer, race-spawned-function, race-spawn-accumulate -- the
spawn's own accumulate, 65 for 97.5 on the GPU -- and race-reducer-read).
Rulings there: the spelling (`spawn atomic x += g(..)` proposed), and
that the renderer's four spawns into the sample's `radiance` would carry
it, so the demotion needs the deferral's fact that a drain's slots are
distinct within a pass to take them off, or they become device atomics.
And a spawned call's drained function spawning onward onto a second queue
(`spawn l += dampen(x, l)` onto `dries`, dampen spawning `soak` onto
`soaks`, both into the iteration's reducer `l`): alone, `[internal]
Error: SSA.cpp:748, soaks!end lists predecessor ^ that does not point to
it` -- the second deferral's one producer is the dries drain's `callc
dampen(...) dries!ran(l)`, whose continuation is the accumulate that
drain owes, and Defer.cpp's single-producer path reads it as the
producer's rest, makes `soaks!end` with `dries!run` as predecessor and
threads the call's value into a record slot from there before the call is
repointed; beside a deferral with a rest it compiles and the inner
spawns' sums are lost (and the first sample's), silently -- `soaks` then
has two producers, the hits drain and the dries drain, and a queue fed by
drains is sized as one drain's capacity (8, the rule for one split
family's leaves, checked as the capacities being equal) for 8 + 8
pushes: 7 and 8 pushes come out right, 11 segfault; with the hits split
as well it dies with SIGBUS, the same overflow on another layout. Not the
drain order, which is right -- hits, dries, soaks, then the rest pass --
as my first reading of it had it. The renderer is exposed to neither: its
radiance is a slot of the `rays` record, not a reducer of the run, and no
spawned call of its chain spawns onward.

### A layout group's base aligned to its largest member (10-12, 14:30-)

**The finding (10-11), the ruling (10-12, 11:50).** A layout's struct is
packed -- its rows are exactly their bytes, the layout language's
promise -- and LLVM's alignment for a packed struct is one, so a whole
row loaded as a value was `load ..., align 1`, which NVPTX, where an
unaligned access is split, made byte loads: ptx/rtiow-primer's 20-byte
node of three floats, a float and two shorts was twenty `ld.global.nc.b8`
and the shifts and ors to put the words back. The user: "a group's base
should be aligned to its largest member, and we should emit aligned
loads as a result."

**Built (CodeGen_LLVM.cpp, runtime/bonsai_buffer.h).**
`ir::layout_member_align(type)` is the most demanding member's alignment
through packed structs and vectors to the scalars (`layout_align` answers
one for a packed struct, which is what each field promises on its own);
`rows_alignment` gives it for an array whose element is a layout struct;
`element_alignment` gives an element of such an array what the base's
promise and the row stride agree on -- their gcd: a 20-byte row on a
four-aligned base is four-aligned at every index, a 48-byte node sixteen
-- and a row's load (the scalar load and the gang's gather, each field's
alignment bounded by the row's) and a row's or a field's store
(`write_alignment`: the promise, the stride, the field offsets along the
write location) carry it; an array that is not a group's rows keeps its
element's ABI alignment. The promise is kept at the boundary:
`unwrap_layout` calls `bonsai_buffer_require_aligned(descriptor, side,
align)` for a group's rows, which checks the buffer starts on the
alignment and refuses it with a message naming the pointer and the
alignment rather than letting a kernel fault -- the runtime's own
allocations are aligned (malloc's sixteen, cudaMalloc's 256), a wrapped
pointer has to be; this is the check the stride-off-the-array rule of
10-11 lacked for plain arrays, where no promise exists. In the primer the
row is five `ld.global.nc.b32` and one `.b16` (fifteen word loads and a
half-word in the program, forty fewer PTX lines, three fewer registers);
26 llvm goldens of the tree and layout tests gained the aligned require
and `align 1 -> 4` (8, 2 where the row says so) on row loads and stores,
nothing else, each read before blessing. The renderer's device
traversal is the RT cores', and its scene arrays are plain arrays, so
nothing of apps/pbrt's kernels changes; apps/rtq's and apps/wosx's GPU
traversals are where this lands, to be measured there.

### `spawn f(args);` and `join;`: the Cilk form built, and the demotion given the drain's slots (10-13, 15:30 - 10-15, 08:45)

**The rulings (10-13, 15:30).** The user, on the two questions the
parallel-semantics document asked: a spawn is `spawn f(args);`, a call
of a void function that reports through its `reduce(op)` arguments --
no `spawn x op= g()`, no `atomic` spelling to invent for it -- and
`join;` is a statement, with the implicit join at a function's return
(and a parfor body's end) that Cilk's sync has at a procedure's return;
cite Cilk. A spawn is a parfor of two iterations in meaning (the call,
the continuation) but the SSA keeps it as its own terminator pair,
Spawn and Join, never lowered to the parfor form, so the deferral and
the analyses see the structure. Every accumulate into a reducer is
atomic by declaration; the compiler takes the atomic off after all
scheduling where the schedule induces no parallelism on it; `atomic`
stays for `mut` locations. A reducer is read only in the scope that
declared it, after the loop or the join. The C++ emitter lowers an
atomic accumulate to std::atomic_ref (nothing is benchmarked through it;
it is the header generator). Do not run heavy suites until the other
session's ablation work is done.

**Built (10-13 evening, 10-15 morning; the machine held by loom-f2's
pinned Souffle timings from 10-13 23:20 to 10-15 00:46).** The language
and IR: Token/Lexer/Parser (`spawn` takes a call; `join`; `atomic` on a
reducer refused; a reducer read refused as a parameter, inside a parfor
declared outside it, and between a spawn it was handed to and the
join), CallStmt::spawned and ir::Join, Accumulate::spawned gone, the SSA
Spawn{call, cont} and Join{next} terminators through every pass and
backend (32 exhaustive visitors, found by building), Defer.cpp's spawn
path on the Spawn terminator (no accumulate continuation, no
acc_field; the reducer stored and handed down like any argument), the
C++ emitter's atomic_ref. The analysis: parameter_contention
(SSA/Contention.cpp), a fixed point over every call site of the program
answering per address parameter of a function called in parallel
whether every concurrent call hands it storage of its own -- the
caller's allocation, the caller's parameter with that answer, or a
record slot the deferral marked distinct -- and DemoteAtomics taking
the atomic off a parameter's address only for Disjoint. The slot fact
(Function::injective_slots, written by the deferral's note_slot, read by
distinct_slot, re-keyed across a split of the drain loop) is recorded
when pushes_at_most_once holds (SSA/DistinctSlots.cpp): the greatest
number of pushes one activity -- an iteration of the owner's innermost
parallel loops: a sample, a drain's entry -- can make onto the queue
before its pass, a longest path over each function's graph with back
edges dropped, through the calls made and the queues drained earlier in
the round, a loop around a push counting many, a push onto a rounds
queue nothing, a recursion many only when a push lies on its cycle.

**What the renderer showed, in order.** The first build of the form kept
sixteen `atom.relaxed.gpu.global.add.f32` in the gpu-wavefront PTX --
four (the vec4 `l`) in each of the shadow, medium_samples, escaped and
emissive kernels -- under the first slot rule, one producer and no other
pusher: the shadow queue has 23 producers (every material kernel pushes
shadow rays), escaped and emissive two each (the routing after the
closest hit, and the medium kernel), hits two. The count over paths
(above) was written for that: two drains feeding one queue are fine
when no path through one sample's work reaches both. Built, it refused
every queue -- "a recursion through _recloop_func0, which pushes" -- the
BVH traversal, recursive and pushing nothing, because a re-entry while
counting answered many outright; now a re-entry answers nothing for
the moment, the function's count becomes many only if it is above zero
and the recursion was hit, and a count taken under an open cycle is
not kept. With that every one of the eleven queues is "distinct within a
pass", and twenty atomics were left (exit_shadow had joined the four
kernels under the stricter rule): medium_samples' four, whose queue had
been distinct from the start. Its accumulate is `l += beta * sigma_a *
...` in vol_medium_step, which the schedule loopify()s and which is
handed `l` by vol_medium_sample; the loop header loopify makes carries
`x`, `n`, `t_maj_in` and names the parameters it does not carry --
`l` among them -- without taking them as arguments, and the definitions
analysis leaves such a name at "unknown here" on purpose (Simplify.cpp's
CSE comment: defer() captures such a value for the continuation that
way), so parameter_of_address answered nothing and the atomic stayed. A
fix in Definitions -- follow the name up the dominator tree -- broke the
renderer's full path integrator instead: the CSE's key for `lam` and
`lambda!loop` became one, it reused `load_field(lambda!loop, 0)` from a
block that does not dominate the use, and codegen reported "@3383 is
not bound in full_path_step"; reverted. The fix is the contention
analysis's alone: Origins::binding_block (a lazily built graph and
dominator tree; the nearest dominating block that takes the name) and
`resolve` looping up to it. Zero `atom.*.add.f32` in the PTX; the 98
`atom.add.u32` left are the queues' counts. Tests at every level for
each: demote-atomics-loopify (ssa, backends/ptx, correctness/gpu:
`series` into an iteration's own `acc` plain, `drip` into the run's
reducer three device atomics with its steps unrolled; 1.75 of each
value, 113.75), and -- found by the compare -- loopify-spawn-mutual
(ssa, correctness/llvm): the megakernel schedules loopify
vol_path_step, which inlines vol_route, which spawns, and the inlined
return had become `join; return` before the caller's return, which
loopify's tail-position walk refused ("its continuation does more than
return"); a join on the way to a return is the return's own, and the
walk sees through it. Suites: 1586 non-GPU and 74 GPU tests pass; every
regenerated golden read.

**Found, not this work's: the megakernel schedules crash on book.**
gpu-optix-mega and gpu-optix-mega-ser abort on pbrt-book/book at every
sample count with CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at the first synchronize,
while they render killeroo-simple and killeroo-gold (images matching
pbrt's) and gpu-optix renders book. The last committed compiler
(3e479342, before this form, built in a worktree) does the same, so the
crash predates the rework; the last compare that ran the megakernel on
book was 2026-10-02's (compare-out-gpu64-storage, 839 ms at 64 spp),
and the schedules were not measured in the twelve days between. Book is
the protocol's one coateddiffuse scene (walk_step.loopify() is in the
megakernel schedules and nowhere else), which is where to look. The
protocol's standing schedule is gpu-optix; this is a debt for the
to-do list, not a blocker.

**Found and fixed (10-15, 16:15): the megakernel crash was the mirror
pass's bookkeeping, not the schedules'.** Bisected to 2b29f205 (the
load narrowing of element reads) and then, one piece of the narrowing at
a time, to the narrowing of `bvh_descend`'s reads of the light tree
alone; the CPU renders identically with and without it, and a
stand-alone descent in a CUDA kernel did not fault, so the fault was
read out of the megakernel's PTX and LLVM IR -- `node_index + 1`
computed before `node_index = 0`, a loop-carried index with `undef`
from the preheader -- and traced into its SSA. The narrowing writes
`cast<u32>(node_index + 1)` once per narrowed field; after the CSE three
of those chains survived in three blocks, and SSA/MirrorLoads.cpp (a
pure value a loop computes from a cell in memory, computed where the
cell is written instead) took each for a chain worth a mirror. The pass
had taken the positions of the cell's writes once per cell and then
processed the candidates one after another, each inserting an
allocation into the entry block and an update after every write, so
from the second candidate on the positions were stale and that mirror's
entry update went in before the cell's own first store: the second and
third mirrors held `cast<u32>(garbage + 1)`, `!else_4` indexed the light
tree with it, and the first tree with an interior node -- book's, with
its several lights; the killeroos' is one leaf, whose descent never
reaches that block -- faulted. The writes are held as the instructions
now and each update is placed at the position the write holds when it
is placed (`position_of`); the sort "from the last position backwards"
is gone. Tests at every level, mirror-derived-loads-twice (ssa,
backends/llvm, correctness/llvm, correctness/gpu): a walk reading a
cell through two chains in two branches, two mirrors of one cell
written at the entry and in the loop; the unfixed compiler shows
`(*i) + 2` before `i = start` in the ssa output, the fixed one both
mirrors from `start`, and the walk's sums are what they should be on
the CPU and the GPU. The whole suite passes (1672 tests); one golden
moved, ssa/alias-edges, a renumbering of the mirror's update
temporaries now that the writes are visited in block order.
walk_step.loopify() was not it. This morning's gpu-optix images, built
by the unfixed compiler, are byte-identical to the fixed megakernels'
(below), so the wavefront's descent was right as compiled then; why its
mirrors came out right where the megakernel's did not is not asked.
